- splits the file into separate embedded tables.

- the total-reports column (row[2]),

request: Analyze the following scientific data pipeline task: Using OMNI2 data, run the NRLMSISE-00 atmospheric model to predict neutral density values for Swarm-B throughout 2024. Derive model inputs (F10.7, F10.7A, daily Ap, 3-hour Ap vector) directly from the OMNI2 dataset. Compare predictions against measured neutral density from Swarm-B POD files and report RMSE over the entire year. Do not use external space weather feeds. OMNI2 data format specification can be found at omni2.text file. 3-hour AP defined according to https://www.mathworks.com/help/aeroblks/nrlmsise00atmospheremodel.html. This requires working with 4 data source(s) and involves approximately 5 processing steps. Domain: astronomy.

subtasks: Read OMNI-2 hourly data files for 2023 and 2024 with fixed field-widths.
Convert the year, day-of-year and hour columns of OMNI-2 into a timezone-aware (UTC) DateTimeIndex, sort chronologically and use it as the time index.

Load every 2024 Swarm-B POD neutral-density text file: skip '#' comment lines, read whitespace-delimited fields, build a time index from the date & time columns (UTC). Keep only the Swarm-B records that occur exactly on the hour (minute = 0, second = 0, microsecond = 0) so they can be matched to the hourly OMNI-2 data.

For any requested model time, derive NRLMSISE-00 driving parameters directly from the indexed OMNI-2 dataframe:
- daily Ap = mean of the 24 hourly Ap values of that day,
- F10.7 = the 00:00 UT row of that day,
- F10.7A = 81-day running mean of daily F10.7 ending the previous day (skip model run when the 81-day window is incomplete),
- 3-hour Ap vector (length 7) generated from the mean Ap of consecutive 3-h bins according to the MATLAB/NRLMSISE specification.
After processing the full year, compute the root-mean-square error between the predicted and observed neutral density values over all timestampls.
